summary: Ignis Atlas is an unofficial, interactive screening aid built on NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. A fire 80,000 miles from home leaves a crew nowhere to go, and lunar habitats are expected to use at least 30% oxygen at 10.2 psi or less. Engineers enter cabin conditions (oxygen, pressure, airflow, gravity, material), and Ignis Atlas shows whether those conditions fall inside, near or outside what NASA's flight experiments recorded, which experiment is closest (with its PSI ID and link), and where no evidence exists. We extracted the experimental tables of 19 ISS and Cygnus combustion investigations. For solid fuels, the highest oxygen recorded in the tables we extracted is 22.2%, and PSI's Reduced Gravity filter returned zero results on 13 November 2026. The tool does not predict fires or certify materials. All data comes from NASA PSI (CC0), cited by investigation ID and DOI; row-by-row verification is in progress.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS:

Ignis Atlas provides deterministic pre-flight screening for spacecraft and lunar surface habitat materials. Users can adjust environmental sliders (O2 concentration 15–100%, cabin pressure 2–16 psi, ventilation airflow, and gravity regimes: 0g, 0.16g Moon, 0.38g Mars, 1.0g Earth). The engine performs a multi-dimensional Euclidean boundary search across NASA PSI flight tables to categorize materials into: COVERED (empirically tested within operational bounds), EXTRAPOLATED (tested in microgravity but ambient conditions or partial gravity exceed bounds), or CRITICAL DATA GAP (zero flight records in PSI).

CREATIVITY & AEROSPACE HUD DESIGN:

- 2D Star-Map Matrix: Interactive scatter visualization mapping tested telemetry bounds against the exploration habitat envelope.

- Flight Material Safety Passport: Real-time correlation linking materials (PMMA, Nomex, Silicone, Cotton-Fiberglass) directly to PSI investigation IDs and DOI resolvers.

- Autonomous Flight Safety Oracle: A multi-step rule-based decision support system evaluating oxygen partial pressure (pO2), gas density shifts, and Minimum Ignition Energy (MIE) depression.

- 3D Morphing Flame Stage: Built with Three.js and custom GLSL shaders illustrating transition from buoyant 1g teardrops to spherical 0g diffusion flames.

BENEFITS & IMPACT:

- Replaces guesswork with empirical ground-truth extracted from NASA flight experiments.

- Demonstrates why Earth-gravity standards (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1) do not directly transfer to lunar gravity.

- Directly supports mission planning for Artemis by justifying payload manifests for planned investigations like LUCI and FM2.

TECHNOLOGIES & TOOLS USED:

- Frontend & Visualization: JavaScript (ES6+), Vite, Three.js, WebGL/GLSL Shaders, GSAP animation engine, SVG.

- Backend & Data Extraction: Python, Pandas, Playwright (for deterministic PSI table harvesting).

- Hosting & Infrastructure: Vercel, GitHub.
